guidance: The add-in host: App.cs (IExternalApplication), EventHandlers, Services (EventService, RibbonService, ApplicationSessionService) and Properties (the Designer files stay; just note them). Look for Revit database logic in the handlers and services that belongs in Kelly-Revit-Logic, reusable framework that belongs in Kelly-Revit-UI, and Revit-free code (project reconciliation, session records, data access) that belongs in Kelly-Domain or Kelly-Windows-Data.

Tools acquired from outside Kelly (Arrange, Vicious). They often re-implement geometry, collector, transaction and string helpers that Kelly-Revit-Logic-v5 or Kelly-Windows already have: look hard for that duplication, and for Revit-free math that belongs in Kelly-Windows or Kelly-Domain.

The files directly in Assigners/ plus four assigner contexts. The six contexts repeat one pattern (about 19 files each): look hard for duplicated logic that one shared Kelly-Revit-Logic-v5 service or one Kelly-Revit-UI base class could own, and compare with the other scope's contexts (ServiceContext, SpoolNumberContext, SystemContext) by reading one of them.

Three assigner contexts, the dockable pane and the reset tool. The six contexts repeat one pattern: look hard for duplicated logic that one shared Kelly-Revit-Logic-v5 service or one Kelly-Revit-UI base class could own, and compare with the other scope's contexts (DetailingPackageContext, LineNumberContext, ModuleNumberContext) by reading one of them.

AllTrade tools. Look for Revit database logic inside commands that belongs in Kelly-Revit-Logic-v5 (layout points, schedules, connectors, tags), Revit-free file, CSV and path code that belongs in Kelly-Windows or Kelly-Domain, and helpers repeated across these tools. Office interop and ExcelDataReader stay in Kelly-Revit.

AllTrade tools. Look for spool, module, support, updater and view-filter logic inside commands and view models that Kelly-Revit-Logic-v5 (Spools, Supports, Updaters, Views) should own, Revit-free spool and naming rules that belong in Kelly-Domain, and helpers repeated across these tools.

AllTrade's ribbon items (panels, push buttons, availability classes) and the module root. Push buttons and availability classes stay with their commands (availability classes must be in the command's assembly); look for repeated button or availability logic that a Kelly-Revit-UI base class should own, and for push buttons that are not beside the command they call.

The PipeTrade and DuctTrade modules. Look for MEP, fabrication and connector logic inside commands that belongs in Kelly-Revit-Logic-v5 (Mep, Fabrication, Connectors), logic the two modules duplicate between them or with AllTrade, and ribbon or availability code a Kelly-Revit-UI base should own.

The Contenter, Manager and Developer modules. Look for family, parameter and project logic inside commands that belongs in Kelly-Revit-Logic, Revit-free data and report code that belongs in Kelly-Domain or Kelly-Windows-Data, and helpers duplicated with AllTrade. Developer tools are diagnostics (WindowMockup, AvailabilityProbe); keep them unless their logic is reusable.

The shared ribbon, command, MVVM, selection-filter and availability framework. Look for Revit database logic that belongs in Kelly-Revit-Logic, Revit-free WPF or prompt helpers that belong in Kelly-Windows, code only one module uses (it belongs in that module, unless it is framework), and namespace/folder mismatches. The abstract command contracts, CommandBase, ViewModel, IView and IViewModel are approved here.

Look for Revit-free code that belongs in Kelly-Domain (or Kelly-Windows), UI concerns that belong in Kelly-Revit-UI or a module, and logic duplicated across the many updater configurations and element services that one shared helper should own. Updater configurations build Revit element services and were judged Revit-bound before; reopen that only for concrete Revit-free parts.

Look for Revit-free code that belongs in Kelly-Domain or Kelly-Windows (generic helpers), data access that belongs in Kelly-Windows-Data, ribbon, command or MVVM code that belongs in Kelly-Revit-UI, and Revit-free parts that can be split out of mixed files. Earlier passes moved about 170 Revit-free files to Kelly-Domain; focus on what is left.

Look for Revit-free code that belongs in Kelly-Domain or Kelly-Windows (generic helpers), data access that belongs in Kelly-Windows-Data, ribbon, command or MVVM code that belongs in Kelly-Revit-UI, and Revit-free parts that can be split out of mixed files. Properties/*.Designer.cs stay. Earlier passes moved about 170 Revit-free files to Kelly-Domain; focus on what is left.

Look for generic non-Kelly code that belongs in Kelly-Windows (converters, math, geometry and fraction helpers), generic caching or data-access code that belongs in Kelly-Windows-Data, WPF IValueConverters (generic: Kelly-Windows; Kelly-specific: stay), anything only Revit-coupled code uses that encodes Revit behaviour (belongs in Kelly-Revit-Logic, only if nothing in Domain or below uses it), and namespace/folder mismatches.

Look for generic non-Kelly code that belongs in Kelly-Windows, data access (SQL, Dapper, stored-procedure calls, JSON persistence) that belongs in Kelly-Windows-Data, WPF IValueConverters, anything only Revit-coupled code uses that encodes Revit behaviour, and namespace/folder mismatches.

Check the Revit-free rule: any mention of Revit concepts or Autodesk types, including XML docs and string literals that encode Revit behaviour. Look for Kelly business concepts that belong in Kelly-Domain (only if nothing in Windows or Windows.Data still uses them), data access in Kelly-Windows that belongs in Kelly-Windows-Data, non-data code in Kelly-Windows-Data-v3 that belongs in Kelly-Windows, and dead or empty folders.

Hunt for duplicated or near-duplicated code ACROSS layers, modules or folders: helper and extension methods, constants, enums, models, converters, colour tables, string/file/path/number helpers, Revit collector and transaction helpers re-implemented in several commands, or re-implementations of something a lower layer already provides. Report each redundant copy as one move: sourceRepo/sourcePath = the copy to remove, targetRepo = the lowest appropriate layer that should own the single implementation, requiredChanges = the callers to repoint and any change the kept copy needs. Only report duplication you have read, not similar names.
